# PROOF OF A CONJECTURE OF FARHI

  * March 2014
  * Asian-European Journal of Mathematics 07(01):1450002

DOI:10.1142/S1793557114500028

Authors:

Gyula Károlyi

  * Eötvös Loránd University


## Abstract

We verify a conjecture of Farhi concerning the growth of a curious arithmetic function defined by 2-adic valuation. We also prove a stronger version suggested by Zhong and Tan.

## Abstract

The semi-topological K-theory of a quasi-projective complex algebraic variety X is based on the notion of algebraic vector bundles modulo algebraic equivalence. This theory is given as the homotopy groups of an infinite loop space which is equipped with maps , whose composition is the natural map from the algebraic K-theory of X to the topological K-theory of the underlying analytic space X^{an} of X. The theory defined and studied here is equivalent (when X is projective and weakly normal) to the so-called “holomorphic K-theory”, , of projective varieties, which is studied by Cohen and Lima-Filho. We give an explicit description of K_{0}^{semi}(X) in terms of K_{0}(X), a description of K_{q}^{semi}(−) in terms of K_{0}^{semi}(−) for projective varieties, a Poincaré duality theorem for projective varieties, and a computation of whenever X is a product of projective spaces or a smooth complete curve. For X a smooth quasi-projective variety, there are natural Chern class maps from to morphic cohomology compatible with similarly defined Chern class maps from algebraic K-theory to motivic cohomology and compatible with the classical Chern class maps from topological K-theory to the singular cohomology of X^{an}.

We formulate the “semi-topological K-theory” of a quasi-projective complex variety X, which we define as the homotopy groups of a certain infinite loop space . This theory interpolates between the algebraic K-theory of X and the topological K-theory of the analytic space X^{an} associated to X, in the sense that there are natural maps of infinite loop spaces (cf. Definition 6.11). Our philosophy is that algebraic K-theory is the study of algebraic vector bundles under rational equivalence, semi-topological K-theory is the study of algebraic vector bundles under algebraic equivalence, and topological K-theory is the study of topological vector bundles under topological equivalence. 
For a smooth variety X, the homotopy invariance of K-theory allows one to think of K_{0}(X) as the group of vector bundles on X modulo “rational equivalence” (i.e., the equivalence relation one gets by taking T to be the affine line in the definition of algebraic equivalence). Ktop(T) = Kst(T)[β−1].
This deﬁnition is of course motivated by the agreement of the Bott inverted Friedlander–Walker
semi-topological K-theory with the usual topological K-theory of complex points (see [FW03, Thm
5.8]), which was also motivated by Thomason’s work on the Bott inverted algebraic K-theory
with ﬁnite coeﬃcients. The point b. in theorem 1.1 is proved by using Riou’s Spanier–Whitehead
duality in the motivic homotopy category of smooth schemes (see prop.4.32). Finally the point d.
of theorem 1.1, namely the construction of the topological Chern map is achieved using Kassel’s
K¨unneth formula for periodic cyclic homology and once again Thm 1.3.
Finally, in §4.3, we give a convenient description of the connective semi-topological K-theory
of any dg-category in terms of the stack MT of perfect T op-dg-modules. This stack is a stack of
E∞-spaces because of the sum of dg-modules. It turns out that its topological realization |MT |
is a group-like E∞-space and one can consider it as a connective spectrum. The proof is based
on the existence of an A1-equivalence between the stack in E∞-spaces MT and the Waldhausen
construction of the category of perfect T op-dg-modules (see Prop 4.17 and Thm 4.21).
